question.text: A PM holds a portfolio with beta 1.2 worth Rs. 40 crore. NIFTY futures contract size is Rs. 2 lakh (fictitious simplification). To hedge the systematic risk fully, how many futures contracts should she short?

explanation.text: The Logic: Hedge ratio = (Portfolio Value × Beta) / Contract Size = (Rs. 40,00,00,000 × 1.2) / Rs. 2,00,000 = Rs. 48,00,00,000 / Rs. 2,00,000 = 2,400 contracts. The Trap: 2000 ignores beta; 3000 over-hedges; 200 uses wrong factor of 10. Cross-Exam Context: VIII has this exact formula; XXI-B applies it at portfolio level. Manager's Pro-Tip: Use realised beta (rolling 60-day) not historical static beta — stale beta leads to under/over-hedge especially in volatile regimes.
